# T20-graph-model

**Goal.** Implement `Graph.from_edges`, `Graph.from_records`, `has_node`, `index_of`, `get_edge`, `has_edge`, `neighbors`, `predecessors`, `adjacency`, `adjacency_matrix`, `weight_matrix`, `reverse`, `relabel` in `src/dsdk/graph/model.py` (`Edge`, `Graph` fields, constants and errors already exist). Build `from_edges` first, run the tests, then the views.

**Files to edit.** `src/dsdk/graph/model.py` only. Do NOT edit any file under `tests/`, `fixtures/`, `tracks.toml`, `tracks/`, or functions owned by other tasks. Read the whole module docstring and every stub docstring first: they are the spec, including exact strings and tie-breaks. Read the tests named in the done command before coding.

**Done when.** `cd /home/user/dsdk && uv run pytest tests/graph/test_graph_model.py -q` passes (69 tests). (exit 0). Also `cd /home/user/dsdk && uv run pytest tests/core tests/logic tests/test_reuse.py -q` must stay green (it passes today).

**Depends on.** none (needs dsdk.core only through `Status`)

**Pitfalls.**
- `from_edges` pipeline, in this order: (1) `edges = list(edges)` and `nodes = None if nodes is None else list(nodes)` (generators may be passed; read each ONCE); (2) validate every item: `Edge` as is, a `tuple` of length 2 or 3 becomes `Edge(*item)`, everything else (a `str` like `"ab"`, a `list`, `None`, an int, a 1-tuple) is `TypeError` -- test `isinstance(item, tuple)` BEFORE `len`; (3) weight: `None` or an `int`/`float` that is NOT a `bool` (`isinstance(True, int)` is true, so check bool first) else `TypeError`; `math.isfinite` else `ValueError`; (4) evidence must be a `Status` (`TypeError`) inside `EDGE_STATUSES` (`ValueError`); (5) label `None` or `str` else `TypeError`; (6) node set; (7) `MissingNodeError` naming the node (use `repr` in the message so `match="ghost"` works); (8) merge; (9) orient and sort.
- Node set: `nodes is None` means first appearance (source then target, per edge, in the order given); otherwise the given order with repeats dropped. Use a dict `{node: index}` for all lookups.
- Merge key: directed `(u, v)`; undirected orient first so `index[u] <= index[v]`, then key `(u, v)`. A self-loop is kept (undirected: key `(u, u)`, stored once). Merge a group of duplicates by: evidence = the entry with the smallest `EVIDENCE_RANK`; weight must be identical for every duplicate (`!=` comparison; `2` versus `None` is a conflict) else `GraphError`; label = `",".join(sorted(distinct non-None labels))` or `None` if there are none.
- Final `edges` tuple is sorted by `(index[source], index[target])`. Build the result with `cls(tuple(nodes), tuple(edges), directed, closed_world)`; `Graph` is a frozen dataclass so do not assign attributes after construction.
- `neighbors(n)`: collect INDICES into a set (directed: targets of edges whose source is `n`; undirected: also sources of edges whose target is `n`), then return the nodes in sorted index order. A self-loop yields `n` once. `predecessors` is the mirror image for directed graphs and equals `neighbors` for undirected ones. Both raise `MissingNodeError` for an absent node; `get_edge` / `has_edge` / `has_node` NEVER raise (absent node: `None` / `False`). Undirected `get_edge(u, v)` must find an edge stored as `(v, u)`.
- `adjacency_matrix` entries are the ints `1` / `0` (not bools), as a tuple of tuples; empty graph gives `()`. `weight_matrix` gives `None` for no edge, `1` for an unweighted edge, the weight otherwise (a weight of `0` stays `0`; do not use truthiness).
- `from_records`: read `r[source]`, `r[target]`, and `r[weight]` / `r[evidence]` / `r[label]` only when those key names are given; any missing key becomes `GraphError` (catch `KeyError`, re-raise `GraphError`). An evidence cell that is a `str` is converted with `Status(cell)` (an unknown string raises `ValueError` by itself; `"invalid"` converts and is then rejected by the normal evidence check). Then call `cls.from_edges(edges, nodes, directed=..., closed_world=...)`.
- `reverse`: undirected returns `self`; directed calls `from_edges` with swapped `Edge`s, `nodes=self.nodes` and the same flags (the re-sort restores the invariants). `relabel`: raise `MissingNodeError` for a node missing from `mapping` BEFORE checking injectivity (`GraphError`); keep every node at its position; build the result directly with `Graph(...)` (positions are unchanged so the edge order stays valid).
- Pure functions: never mutate `self`; the tests check hashing and equality of results.

Remove `raise NotImplementedError` only in the functions this task owns. Keep docstrings and the existing imports. Standard library only.
